stem.text: The number of people waiting in a line, measured in people, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function N of time t, measured in minutes. It is known that \( N'(5) = -2.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( N'(5) = -2.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 5 minutes, the number of people in the line is decreasing at a rate of 2.5 people per minute.

worked_solution.text: \( N'(5) \) is the rate of change of the number of people in the line at the instant t = 5, so it is measured in people per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: derivative as a rate of change

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so the number of people in the line is decreasing at that instant, by 2.5 people for each minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction

options.label: At time t = 5 minutes, the number of people in the line has changed by a total of -2.5 people.
options.derivation: the derivative value read as an amount, the total change in the quantity, rather than a rate

options.label: At time t = 5 minutes, the number of people in the line is increasing at a rate of 2.5 people per minute.
options.derivation: the negative rate reported as its magnitude and described as an increase

options.label: At time t = 5 minutes, the number of people in the line is decreasing at a rate of 2.5 minutes per person.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over quantity units

options.label: At time t = 5 minutes, the number of people in the line is decreasing at a rate of 2.5 people per minute.
